title: Survey of wastes management status of Khayyam industrial estate in Neyshabur City (Northeastern Iran) in 2017
author: Alidadi, Mohammadi, et al.

steps.title: Record site geographic and climate data
steps.instruction: Note that the study site is Khayyam Industrial Estate in Neyshabur, Iran, located at 36° 10′ N, 58° 50′ E, 20 km from the Neyshabur‑Mashhad road. The estate covers 246 ha and contains 144 active industries. The city is 100 km from Sabzevar and 120 km from Mashhad, has a population of 451,780, highest temperature 40.5 °C, lowest –20 °C, average annual temperature 14.8 °C and average precipitation 365.8 mm / year.

steps.title: Define study area and industry count
steps.instruction: Confirm that the industrial estate area is 246 ha with 144 active industries and that it is one of the largest estates in Khorasan Razavi province.

steps.title: Classify industries into EPA groups
steps.instruction: Classify the industries into the 10 groups defined by the Iranian Environmental Protection Agency: food & pharmaceutical, textile, wood & cellulose, paper, plastic & chemical, non‑metallic, metal, machinery, cosmetics, and electronic.

steps.title: Administer standard waste questionnaire
steps.instruction: Use the standard questionnaire designed by the Iranian Environmental Protection Agency (25 questions, 4 sections: basic information, quality, quantity, waste management). Have knowledgeable personnel (environmental health experts or managers) complete one questionnaire for each of the 144 active industries, visiting industrial units on selected days each week following a daily path.

steps.title: Select largest units for sampling
steps.instruction: From each of the 10 industry groups, select the 10 largest industrial units (based on the EPA classification) for quantitative waste sampling, giving a total of 100 sampled units.

steps.title: Mix waste thoroughly in each unit
steps.instruction: At the end of the working day, completely mix the waste in each selected unit using a shovel or other device to ensure homogeneity and to eliminate coarse components.

steps.title: Collect and divide waste sample
steps.instruction: From the well‑mixed waste, take a sample from a point lacking coarse components, divide the mixed waste into three equal parts, and remove exactly 1 kg from one of the parts.

steps.title: Weigh sample with precision scale
steps.instruction: Weigh the 1 kg sample on a Sartorius GE812 laboratory balance with 0.01 g precision, wearing gloves and a mask for safety.

steps.title: Separate and identify waste components
steps.instruction: Physically separate the weighed sample into its constituent components (e.g., paper, plastic, metal, etc.) and record the mass of each component.

steps.title: Calculate component percentages and economic value
steps.instruction: Calculate the percentage of each component relative to the total sample weight and compute the economic value of recyclable components using price data from the Iranian Waste Management Organization.

steps.title: Analyze data with SPSS
steps.instruction: Enter all questionnaire responses and sample composition data into SPSS version 18, then perform statistical analysis to assess waste‑management status of the industrial estate.

steps.title: Create charts using Excel
steps.instruction: Export the analysis results from SPSS and generate visual charts in Microsoft Excel to illustrate waste quantities, compositions, and economic values.
